holderRole: Peter de Florez Professor of Economics and Computer Science, MIT

items.title: Science in the Age of Algorithms
items.detail: A public panel welcoming Professor Mullainathan as Sanjaya Lall Visiting Professor of Business and Development, on what algorithmic systems are doing to the practice of science itself.
items.people: Sir Nigel Shadbolt (Principal of Jesus College and Professor of Computer Science, Oxford), Sendhil Mullainathan (MIT), and Dr Raia Hadsell (VP of Research, Google DeepMind). Chaired by Professor Johannes Abeler, Head of the Department of Economics.
items.venue: Andrew Wiles Building, Mathematical Institute · 5.00pm, followed by a drinks reception

items.title: The Sanjaya Lall Lecture 2026
items.detail: What large language models can and cannot do is usually treated as a question for computer scientists. Mullainathan argues that economists are uniquely equipped to answer it.
items.venue: Lecture Theatre, Manor Road Building · 5.00–6.30pm, followed by a drinks reception

holderRole: Henry J. Heinz II Professor of Economics and Director of the Economic Growth Center, Yale University

items.title: The Sanjaya Lall Lecture 2025
items.detail: Delivered during Professor Pande's Trinity Term visit. Her research examines how institutions shape economic, political, and environmental inequality in low- and middle-income countries.
items.people: Rohini Pande (Yale University), an alumna of the Oxford PPE programme
items.venue: University of Oxford · Hosted by the Department of Economics

holderRole: Institute Professor, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

items.title: The Future of Work in the Age of AI
items.detail: A public panel on what artificial intelligence means for employment, wages, and the organisation of work — the question closest to the CTS research agenda.
items.people: Sir Christopher Pissarides (Regius Professor of Economics, LSE, and Nobel laureate), Daron Acemoglu (MIT), and Helen Margetts (Professor of Internet and Society, Oxford). Q&A chaired by Professor Sir John Vickers.
items.venue: Nelson Mandela Lecture Theatre, Saïd Business School · 5.00pm, followed by a reception. Co-sponsored by Saïd Business School and St John's College

items.title: The Sanjaya Lall Memorial Lecture 2024
items.detail: Drawing on Power and Progress, Acemoglu challenged the idea that technological advance leads naturally to greater prosperity — what he calls the 'productivity bandwagon' — arguing that who benefits depends on institutions and choices rather than on technology itself.
items.venue: University of Oxford · Hosted by the Saïd Business School

items.title: Green Industrial Policy: Saving the World without a Trade War
items.detail: A public panel welcoming Professor Stiglitz as Sanjaya Lall Distinguished Visiting Fellow, on whether decarbonisation and open trade can be reconciled.
items.people: Joseph Stiglitz (Columbia), Professor Lord Nicholas Stern, the Hon. Ed Miliband MP, and Michael Liebreich.
items.venue: Andrew Wiles Building, Mathematical Institute · 5.00pm, discussion and Q&A followed by a reception. Co-sponsored by the Department of Economics

items.title: Freedom and Liberty: Perspectives from 21st Century Economics
items.detail: The Sanjaya Lall Memorial Fund Lecture 2023, revisiting the concept of freedom through the lens of contemporary economics.

items.venue: Mathematical Institute · 5.30–7.00pm. Hosted by the Department of Economics

items.title: Creating Equality of Opportunity: New Insights from Big Data
items.detail: On what administrative and social-network data reveal about why children's chances of upward mobility vary so sharply across neighbourhoods.

items.detail: Duflo drew on research into school learning techniques in rural India that bridges economics with psychology and cognitive science; the panellists responded from their own experience of large-scale policy interventions.

items.detail: A public panel welcoming Professor Dixit as Sanjaya Lall Visiting Professor, on the rise of firms from developing economies as global multinationals — a subject at the centre of Sanjaya Lall's own research.
items.people: Professor Tim Besley (School Professor of Economics and Political Science, LSE), Avinash Dixit (Princeton), and Professor Robert Wade (Professor of Political Economy and Development, LSE, and the first holder of the Professorship).
